EXECUTIVE ORDER 2019-001

DIRECTIVE TO THE STATE PUBLIC EDUCATION DEPARTMENT TO IMMEDIATELY TAKE
THE STEPS NECESSARY TO BEGIN TRANSITIONING AWAY FROM USE OF THE
STANDARDIZED TEST TERMED THE "PARTNERSHIP FOR ASSESSMENT OF READINESS FOR
COLLEGE AND CAREERS" (""PARCC") AND TO WORK WITH STAKEHOLDERS TO IDENTIFY
AND IMPLEMENT A MORE EFFECTIVE METHOD FOR ASSESSING SCHOOL PERFORMANCE

WHEREAS, as Governor, I am committed to making immediate improvements to our Public Education
system.

WHEREAS, students throughout New Mexico have been required to take the PARCC, which is a test
purported to serve as an accountability measure for New Mexico School Districts and Charter Schools in the
areas of English Language Arts and Mathematics. The PARCC test is given to students in grades 3-11.

WHEREAS, PARCC has been widely criticized as being expensive, ineffective, and a poor performance
measure for schools and students. For these reasons, many states around the country have discontinued or are in
the process of discontinuing the use of PARCC testing. Lt. Governor, Howie Morales, who holds a Ph.D. in
Education, has pointed out that "PARCC is a colossal and expensive failure for our State" and that “[t]here are
better ways to assess the learning of school-age children." Lt. Governor Morales’ observations are consistent
with empirical data. PARCC testing accounts for 90% of the ratings and assessments that New Mexico
elementary and middle schools receive, and 75% of the ratings and assessments that New Mexico high schools
receive. Consequently, teachers and administrators are unreasonably forced to expend excessive resources

preparing students to take the PARCC test. The result is that New Mexico students spend too much time being

“taught to the test” and not enough time learning.

THE STEPS NECESSARY TO BEGIN TRANSITIONING AWAY FROM USE OF THE

WHEREAS, as Governor, I am committed to making immediate improvements to our Public Education
system.

WHEREAS, PARCC is a test purported to serve as an accountability measure for New Mexico School
Districts and Charter Schools.

WHEREAS, as addressed in Executive Order 2019-001, PARCC has been widely criticized as being
expensive, ineffective, and a poor performance measure for schools, students, and teachers.

WHEREAS, I am committed to implementing a sounder methodology for the rating and assessments of
New Mexico educators. To identify, develop, and implement an alternative approach, we must have input from
our Public Education Department, teachers, administrators, parents, students, and recognized professionals and
experts in the field of teacher assessments. Through this collaborative approach, New Mexico can develop
means for conducting meaningful evaluation of our teachers.

THEREFORE, for these reasons discussed above, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of

New Mexico, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New

Mexico, do hereby ORDER and DIRECT:

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2019-003

EXECUTIVE ORDER ON ADDRESSING CLIMATE CHANGE AND ENERGY WASTE
PREVENTION

I. Background and Purpose

To further New Mexico’s responsibility and opportunity to build a clean energy future for our
people, limit adverse climate change impacts that harm our natural and cultural heritage, prevent
the waste of New Mexico energy resources and reduce pollution that threatens human health, |
hereby issue this Executive Order.

Il. Climate Change

WHEREAS, climate change creates new risks and exacerbates existing vulnerabilities in
communities across New Mexico and presents growing challenges for human health and safety,
quality of life, and the rate of economic growth.

WHEREAS, in a special report authored by the United Nations and World Meteorological
Organization Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (“IPCC”), it was found that the planet
has as little as 12 years to take meaningful climate action in order to limit the increase in global
average temperature to 1.5°C — the level necessary to forestall dramatic climatic changes that
will further imperil our water supplies.

WHEREAS, carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs),
perfluorocarbons, and sulfur hexafluoride are recognized as the six greenhouse gases
contributing to climate change.

WHEREAS, in 2009, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) found that these “six
greenhouse gases taken in combination endanger both the public health and the public welfare of
current and future generations.”

WHEREAS, in May 2010, the National Research Council, the operating arm of the National
Academy of Sciences, published an assessment which concluded that “climate change is
occurring, is caused largely by human activities, and poses significant risks for - and in many
cases is already affecting - a broad range of human and natural systems.”

WHEREAS, carbon dioxide is emitted through the combustion of fossil fuels for electricity
generation and for combustion-engine vehicles.

WHEREAS, the U.S. Energy Information Administration finds that the transportation sector is
the largest anthropogenic source of carbon dioxide emissions in the United States.

WHEREAS, methane is a powerful greenhouse gas, 84 times more effective at trapping heat than
carbon dioxide over a 20-year timeframe.

WHEREAS, the oil and gas industry is the largest industrial source of methane emissions.

WHEREAS, HFCs are potent greenhouse gases used in the refrigeration, air c

market.

EMNRD and NMED shall jointly develop a statewide, enforceable regulatory framework to
secure reductions in oil and gas sector methane emissions and to prevent waste from new and
existing sources and enact such rules as soon as practicable.

EMNRD and NMED shall coordinate as much as possible with the New Mexico State Land
Office and federal bureaus and agencies that manage land and natural resources in New
Mexico to help advance the priorities identified in this Executive Order.

The Climate Change Task Force will develop a New Mexico Climate Strategy document with
initial recommendations and a status update, where applicable, to the Governor by September
15, 2019.


IV. Disclaimer

Nothing in this Executive Order is intended to create a private right of action to enforce any
provision of this Order or to mandate the undertaking of any particular action pursuant to this
Order; nor is this Order intended to diminish or expand any existing legal rights or remedies.

THIS ORDER supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives in conflict.
This Executive Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until such time as it
is rescinded by the Governor.

A MEMORIAL RECOGNIZING THE HONORABLE HENRY “KIKI” SAAVEDRA

WHEREAS, the Honorable Henry “Kiki” Saavedra served this State and his community for thirty-
eight (38) years in the New Mexico House of Representatives. In that capacity, and in his personal life,
Representative Saavedra positively impacted those around him.

WHEREAS, the entire State of New Mexico is better off for Representative Saavedra’s good work,
and his death constitutes a grave loss for our State’s residents.

WHEREAS, it is appropriate and proper to publicly acknowledge Representative Saavedra’s
efforts through a public day of mourning across New Mexico.

THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by virtue of the
authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby ORDER
and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-mast through sundown of February 6", 2019 through
sundown of February 8", 2019. This action will serve to honor Representative Saavedra and to mourn his
loss.

WHEREAS, since 1947 the Public Employees Retirement Association of New Mexico
(“PERA”) has provided a defined retirement benefit to hundreds of thousands of New Mexico
public employees and their families.

WHEREAS, PERA is a significant contributor to the State of New Mexico’s economy and
has paid $1.2 billion in benefits in 2018 to more than 40,000 current retirees, with over 90% of
that amount remaining in communities across New Mexico.

WHEREAS, due to benefit enhancements made in the late 1990s that were not properly
funded and the Great Recession in 2007, PERA, like virtually all public pension plans in America,
experienced declines in its Trust Fund balance that necessitated the passage of pension reform by
the New Mexico Legislature in 2013 (“the 2013 reforms”).

WHEREAS, the 2013 reforms improved the fiscal condition of the PERA Fund by
requiring shared sacrifice among all PERA membership groups, including active employees and
retirees.

WHEREAS, the 2013 reforms also required that the state, municipalities, counties and
other political subdivisions increase their contributions to PERA.

WHEREAS, the PERA Board of Trustees has taken prudent actions since 2013, such as

lowering the long-term investment assumption used to value PERA’s liabilities, and the Executive,

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2019-007
ESTABLISHING THE NEW MEXICO 2020 COMPLETE COUNT COMMISSION

I. Background and Need

WHEREAS, the U.S. Constitution (Article 1, Section 2) mandates a headcount every 10
years of everyone residing in the 50 states, Puerto Rico, and the Island Areas of the United States.

WHEREAS, research indicates that approximately 43 percent of New Mexico’s population
live in “hard-to-count” areas. For this reason, New Mexico’s population is difficult to accurately
tally. Adequate resources are therefore required to ensure that New Mexicans living in “hard-to-
count” communities are not overlooked.

WHEREAS, a complete count is key to ensuring New Mexico receives its fair share of
federal assistance. New Mexico loses approximately $3,700 for every one of our State’s residents
who goes uncounted. These losses may be significant in the aggregate. A one percent undercount
in the decennial Census would result in the loss of $780 million over ten years.

WHEREAS, in addition to the impact on federal dollars, an inaccurate undercount may
yield unequal political representation and a corresponding decline in access to resources, as both
Congressional apportionment and state legislative redistricting are based on the decennial Census.

WHEREAS, an accurate Census count provides reliable data that businesses, governments,
hospitals, and other institutions use for planning, development and investment.

WHEREAS, in recent decades, New Mexico has struggled to achieve a complete count. In

A MEMORIAL RECOGNIZING THE HONORABLE JOHN PINTO

WHEREAS, the Honorable John Pinto served his country and this State for more than four
decades as a State Senator and as a United State Marine and Navajo Code Talker during the Second
World War. During his long and legendary life, Senator Pinto tirelessly advocated for his local
community and for native communities throughout New Mexico.

WHEREAS, the entire State of New Mexico has benefitted from Senator Pinto’s storied
career of personal sacrifice and public service. His death is a grave loss for our State.

WHEREAS, it is appropriate and proper to publicly acknowledge Senator Pinto’s work on
behalf of New Mexicans through a public day of mourning across New Mexico.

THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff from sundown of May 24, 2019
through sundown of May 28, 2019. This action will honor Senator Pinto’s life and mourn his loss.

wellness.

policy template for departments and agencies to implement.

WHEREAS, the purpose of this Order is to commemorate the victims of two recent
mass shootings, to express support for the survivors and family members of victims and
survivors, and to bring awareness to the fact that such senseless acts of violence are far too
common in our communities and constitute a crisis that we must end;

WHEREAS, twenty people were killed and dozens more were wounded when a shooter
opened fire at a shopping center in El Paso, Texas, on August 3, 2019 (“El Paso shooting”);

wounded when a shooter opened fire on a busy street in Dayton, Ohio, in the early morning
hours on August 4, 2019 (“Dayton shooting”);

WHEREAS, the State of New Mexico stands with the victims of these horrifying acts
of violence and their family members, and salutes the bravery of the law enforcement officers
who swiftly responded to these tragedies and prevented further loss of life; and

WHEREAS, it is important to publicly honor and mourn the individuals who were killed
in the El Paso and Dayton shootings, to express support for the surviving victims and family
members of victims, and to acknowledge and remember the untenable public health crisis of

gun violence in this country.

THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by

virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New

Mexico, hereby ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff effective

immediately through sundown on August 7, 2019. This action will commemorate those

who were killed or wounded in the El Paso shooting and the Dayton shooting and will serve

to remind us that we must do more to prevent such tragedies in the future.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2020-041

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF TO COMMEMORATE JUNETEENTH
FREEDOM DAY AND TO RECOGNIZE VICTIMS OF RACISM AND HATE

This Order commemorates Juneteenth Freedom Day, which is an official State holiday
recognizing the importance of African Americans as American citizens and New Mexico residents.

The purpose of Juneteenth Freedom Day is to reflect on the history of African-American
slavery in the United States, including the experience of Africans brought to the United States in
a five- to twelve-week journey across the Atlantic; the deaths of thousands of Africans who died
in inhuman conditions of passage; the abuse of African-American slaves, including whipping,
castration, branding, and rape; and the importance of the Thirteenth Amendment to the United
States Constitution abolishing slavery throughout the United States and its territories.

Juneteenth occurs on June 19th of each year to honor June 19, 1865, the day on which a
message regarding the abolition of slavery is said to have reached the western states. In New
Mexico, pursuant to NMSA 1978, Section 12-5-14, Juneteenth Freedom Day is observed on the
third Saturday of June, which is June 20th this year.

The abolition of slavery in the United States is an important milestone worthy of
celebration but, unfortunately, we have not come close to fully eradicating its pernicious impacts
on society. We must acknowledge that racism and racial inequalities — and the hatred and violence
through which they are too often exercised — are still pervasive in the United States and they take

many forms.

have failed to overcome the legacy of slavery by recognizing individuals who have been victims
of racism and hate. We must stand together to listen to them and their advocates, and to honor

of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby

victims of racism and hate throughout our State and the United States.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2021-028

DECLARING A DROUGHT AND SEVERE FIRE CONDITIONS THROUGHOUT THE
STATE OF NEW MEXICO AND URGING MUNICIPAL AND COUNTY
GOVERNMENTS TO CONSIDER FIREWORK BANS UNDER THE FIREWORKS
LICENSING AND SAFETY ACT

WHEREAS, in recent weeks, fire danger has increased throughout the State due to warmer
temperatures, lower humidity, high winds, and an abundance of dry, fine fuels;

WHEREAS, according to the United States Drought Monitor, approximately 88% of New
Mexico is experiencing severe drought conditions, while more than half the State is experiencing
extreme to exceptional drought conditions;

WHEREAS, significant fire danger and prevailing drought conditions create the
possibility for numerous natural disasters, including severe wildfires, flooding due to severe
wildfires, and crop production loss;

WHEREAS, federal authorities enacted early measures to respond to increased fire danger
in the State by issuing Stage I and Stage II fire restrictions on many federal lands in April and May
of 2021:

WHEREAS, many tribal governments have also acted swiftly to impose fire restrictions

on their lands, including the Mescalero Apache Tribe and the Navajo Nation; and

WHEREAS, since May of 2021, several wildfires have been burning throughout the State.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico
do hereby DECLARE drought and severe fire conditions exist throughout New Mexico and
URGE New Mexico’s counties, municipalities, and local governments to consider implementing
appropriate firework bans pursuant to the Fireworks Safety and Licensing Act, NMSA 1978, §§
60-2C-1 to -11, as well as any other appropriate fire prevention measures that they may legally
enact.

extent they are in conflict.

Conservation Act, NMSA 1978, Sections 68-2-1 to -25;

supplies, and contract services for aircraft and equipment, and the majority of these expenditures
are with state vendors, local government, and federal agencies;

WHEREAS, the Forestry Division is designated as the agent of the State and authorized
to enter into contracts and agreements with the Secretary of Agriculture of the United States and

pursuant to NMSA 1978, Section 68-2-6; and

health, safety, and welfare.

by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico
do hereby DECLARE an emergency situation exists and ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2022-096

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF IN MEMORIAL
OF LANCE CORPORAL EVAN STRICKLAND

Lance Corporal Evan Strickland, of Valencia County, tragically passed away in an Osprey
aircraft crash during training with the U.S. Marines on Wednesday, June 8, 2022. Lance Corporal
Strickland honorably served his State and his Nation as a U.S. Marine. Lance Corporal Strickland’s
bravery and service will endure, and he will be greatly missed by his community. It is appropriate
and proper to acknowledge Lance Corporal Strickland’s life and service through a public period
of mourning across New Mexico.

NOW THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
do hereby ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff beginning June 14,
2022, and lasting through sundown of June 16, 2022. This action will serve to commemorate Lance

Corporal Strickland’s life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2022-152

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NUDOT’s assistance remains;

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol * Room400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New
Mexico, and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
including NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, do hereby DECLARE an emergency situation
exists and ORDER and DIRECT:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extend they are in conflict.

a This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until renewed,
modified, or rescinded.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2022-164

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF IN MEMORY
OF HIROSHI “HERSHEY” MIYAMURA

On November 29, 2022, Congressional Medal of Honor recipient and native New Mexican
Hiroshi “Hershey” Miyamura passed away at the age of 97. Born in Gallup, New Mexico, Hiroshi
joined the U.S. Army during World War II in January 1945 as part of the all-Nisei 100th Infantry
Battalion, 442nd Infantry Regiment, which was composed mostly of Japanese Americans. After
serving honorably for the remainder of World War II, Miyamura was again asked to serve his
country during the Korean War. On April 24, 1951, while occupying a defensive position that was
on the verge of being overrun, then-Cpl. Miyamura bravely engaged in intense hand-to-hand
combat to fight off the assault so he could administer first aid and direct the evacuation of his
squad members. When another assault came, he ordered his squad to evacuate while he stayed
behind fighting off the advancing soldiers until he was severely wounded and captured. He
remained a prisoner of war for over two years. Upon return to the U.S. after his release from
capture, Miyamura worked for the U.S. Post Office in Gallup. On October 27, 1953, President
Dwight D. Eisenhower presented Miyamura with the Medal of Honor for his bravery. Our country
and the State of New Mexico owe Miyamura an immense debt of gratitude, and his bravery and

public dedication will not be forgotten.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-015

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NMDOT’s assistance remains;

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol * Room400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New
Mexico, and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
including NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, do hereby DECLARE an emergency situation
exists and ORDER and DIRECT:

1, The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extend they are in conflict.

3. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until renewed,

modified, or rescinded.

AMENDED ORDER ESTABLISHING THE PUBLIC REGULATION
COMMISSION TRIBAL ADVISORY COUNCIL

WHEREAS, the Public Regulation Commission (the ““PRC”) is an important entity that

regulates utilities and other public service companies to ensure the provision of adequate services
at fair and reasonable rates;

WHEREAS, since its creation in 1996, the PRC consisted of a five-member commission

whereby each commissioner is elected from a region of the State;

WHEREAS, this districtwide election system allowed for Native American communities
to have consistent representation on the PRC;

WHEREAS, in 2020, the people of New Mexico ratified the Legislature’s proposal to

amend the New Mexico Constitution to transition the PRC commissioner selection process from

districtwide elections to appointment by the Governor from a list of nominees submitted by the
PRC Nominating Committee;

WHEREAS, the 2020 amendment also reduced the size of the PRC from five
commissioners to three commissioners;

WHEREAS, these changes make it difficult to ensure a continuity of Native American
representation on the PRC;

representation given how important the PRC’s work is to the Native American community; and

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-019
ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF IN MEMORIAL
OF THE HONORABLE J. PAUL TAYLOR
On February 12, 2023, the Honorable J. Paul Taylor passed away at the age of 102.
Representative Taylor served the State and his community in the New Mexico House of
Representatives for eighteen years as the “conscience of the Legislature.” A longtime educator,
Representative Taylor was known for championing New Mexico’s people and culture.
Representative Taylor is a true state treasure, and his legacy of service will endure. It is appropriate
and proper to acknowledge Representative Taylor’s remarkable life and service through a public
period of mourning across New Mexico.
THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff beginning February 13, 2023, and
lasting though sundown of February 15, 2023. This action will serve to commemorate
Representative Taylor’s distinguished life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-038

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF PRESIDENT PETERSON ZAH

On March 7, 2023, President Peterson Zah passed away at the age of 85. President Zah’s
remarkable life and long career were dedicated to service of others and correcting wrongdoings
against Native Americans. He will be remembered for his passion, his humility, and his
selflessness. He will also be remembered as the Navajo Nation’s first president, having been
inaugurated in January 1991. President Zah was an inspirational and compassionate man, leading
with humility and instilling hope in his communities. President Zah’s legacy will endure, and the
effects of his life’s work felt by many generations to come. It is appropriate and proper to
acknowledge President Zah’s life and service through a public period of mourning across New
Mexico.

THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff beginning March 14, 2023, and
lasting though sundown of March 15, 2023. This action will serve to commemorate President

Zah’s distinguished life and to mourn his loss.

as a devoted public servant with a great sense of humor and having true love for his people and
family. It is appropriate and proper to acknowledge President Shelly’s life and legacy through a
public period of mourning across New Mexico.

Jerry Apodaca, Governor of New Mexico from 1975-1979, passed away on April 26, 2023,
at age 88. Taking office after already having served in the New Mexico Senate for eight years,
Governor Apodaca notably reorganized New Mexico government into the structure we recognize
today: a cabinet system with department heads. Apodaca will be remembered for pushing for
reforms in education, advocating for patients with chronic pain, and being instrumental in creation
of the State’s first medical cannabis program, as well as being one the first governors to regularly
appoint women and people of color into leadership roles in New Mexico. In 1978, Apodaca was
appointed as Chair of the President’s Council on Physical Fitness by President Jimmy Carter.

But Governor Apodaca’s greatest legacy arguably stems from the years after he served in
office. He was an advisor and role model for generations of Hispanic leaders, politicians, and
business owners—roles in which he took pride and took seriously. Determined and gritty, Apodaca
worked to make places and positions more accessible to minorities who historically rarely had
such access. He also became involved in publishing Hispanic-audience periodicals and served as
a member of the University of New Mexico Board of Regents from 1985 to 1991. The headquarters
building for the New Mexico Department of Education was renamed for Apodaca in 2004.

Governor Apodaca will be remembered as a historic leader and as a man who truly made
an impact on the world by paving the way for many more New Mexicans to enter public office

and become leaders in our State and around the country. It is appropriate and proper to

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-063

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NMDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol * Room400 «+ Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE an emergency situation exists and ORDER and DIRECT:

l. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, and welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

Dy This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extent they are in conflict.

3 This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until renewed,
modified, or rescinded.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2023-090

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, two of the larger wildfires, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires, have left
substantial burn scars placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the New Mexico Department of Transportation plays a vital role in
addressing this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora
County and San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding authorized to address this emergency is nearly depleted,
but the urgent need for the Department of Transportation’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to require the resources of
the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm, and it remains necessary to take
immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives and

property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol - Room 400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 + 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New
Mexico and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution, by
virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the State of New Mexico
do hereby DECLARE an emergency situation exists and ORDER and DIRECT:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred fifty thousand dollars ($750,000.00)
to the Department of Transportation in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25,
and NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of
avoiding or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, and
welfare; and providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of
any expenses incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil
authorities. Such funds shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and
Administration upon vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

I FURTHER ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until all

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF PRESIDENT EDWARD VELARDE

On May 12, 2024, President Edward Velarde of the Jicarilla Apache Nation passed away
at the age of 76. He served as the Jicarilla Apache Nation president since 2019. President Velarde
was a committed and effective leader who sought to strengthen state-tribal relations. He will be
remembered for his tireless advocacy, leadership, and commitment to his tribal community and
the state of New Mexico. President Velarde’s legacy will endure, and the effects of his life’s work
felt by many generations to come. It is appropriate and proper to acknowledge President Velarde’s
life and service through a public period of mourning across New Mexico.

NOW THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
do hereby ORDER and DIRECT that all state flags be flown at half-staff beginning May 15,
2024, and lasting though sundown of May 16, 2024. This action will serve to commemorate

Jicarilla Apache Nation President Edward Velarde’s distinguished life and to mourn his loss.

Agriculture and other state, federal, and private agencies or organizations to prevent and suppress

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2024-096

AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR NEW MEXICO
NATIONAL GUARD DEPLOYMENTS IN FISCAL YEARS 2024 AND 2025

WHEREAS, when resources of the New Mexico National Guard are needed in support of
civil emergencies and disasters, including search and rescue missions, this support must be
immediately deployable;

WHEREAS, funding for National Guard assets must be in place prior to any mission
assignment to assure a rapid and unhindered deployment in time of need; and

WHEREAS, the funding previously authorized for the National Guard to fulfill such
missions is nearly depleted.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
do hereby ORDER, pursuant to NMSA 1978, Sections 20-1-4(A), (D), -6, NMSA 1978, Section
20-2-3(A), and NMSA 1978, Section 20-4-3(A), into service any elements of the New Mexico
National Guard that are, or may be necessary to provide support to civilian authorities in any
county of the State of New Mexico in response to civil emergencies, disasters, or search and rescue

missions.

health crisis on June 25, 2024:

WHEREAS, according to the United States Surgeon General, 54% of adults in America
report that either they or a family member have been threatened with a firearm, killed by a firearm,
witnessed someone being shot, shot someone in self-defense, or injured by a firearm;

WHEREAS, New Mexico consistently has some of the highest rates of gun violence in
the nation:

WHEREAS, New Mexico’s gun death rates rose from seventh highest nationwide in 1999
to third highest in 2021, with the age-adjusted gun death rate increasing by 87% between 2010 and
2021;

WHEREAS, the rate of gun deaths in New Mexico increased 43% from 2009 to 2018,
compared to an 18% increase over this same time period nationwide;

WHEREAS, 550 New Mexicans died as a result of gun violence in 2022, and the
Department of Health estimates that gun death rates in New Mexico will continue to be

significantly higher than rates for the United States as a whole in 2023;

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2024-201
AUTHORIZING ADDITIONAL EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR
THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION DUE TO WILDFIRES
AND FLOODING IN SAN MIGUEL AND MORA COUNTIES

WHEREAS, the State recently experienced numerous wildfires that have destroyed
hundreds of structures, burnt hundreds of thousands of acres, and displaced many New Mexicans;

WHEREAS, the Governor has issued numerous executive orders declaring emergencies
relating to some of these wildfires, including Executive Orders 2022-017, 2022-018, 2022-019,
2022-020, 2022-021, 2022-025, 2022-076, 2022-077, and 2022-087;

WHEREAS, the Hermits Peak and Calf Canyon fires have left substantial burn scars
placing San Miguel County and Mora County at risk of devastating flooding;

WHEREAS, the Department of Transportation (NMDOT) plays a vital role in addressing
this ongoing emergency with debris removal and flood response assistance for Mora County and
San Miguel County roads and property;

WHEREAS, the previous funding to address this emergency is nearly depleted, but the
urgent need for NMDOT’s assistance remains; and

WHEREAS, the continuing emergency is of such magnitude as to be beyond local control
and require the resources of the State of New Mexico to minimize economic or physical harm and
to take immediate action necessary to protect the peace, health, and safety and to preserve the lives

and property of the people of the State of New Mexico.

State Capitol - Room 400 +¢ Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 * 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE an emergency situation exists in San Miguel and Mora Counties due to wildfires and
flooding and ORDER and DIRECT:

l. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency
financial resources in an amount not to exceed seven hundred and fifty thousand dollars
($750,000.00) to the NMDOT in accordance with NMSA 1978, Sections 12-11-23 to -25, and
NMSA 1978, Sections 12-10-14 to -15. Such funds shall be expended for the purposes of avoiding
or minimizing economic and physical harm; protecting the public health, safety, and welfare; and
providing emergency and disaster relief, including, but not limited to, the payment of any expenses
incident to the provision of humanitarian relief and other assistance to civil authorities. Such funds
shall be paid out upon warrants drawn by the Secretary of Finance and Administration upon
vouchers approved by the Governor or her Authorized Representative.

2. This Order supersedes any other previous orders, proclamations, or directives to the
extent they are in conflict.

3. This Order shall take effect immediately and shall remain in effect until all

authorized funds are expended or no longer necessary to provide emergency assistance.

DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY AND EMERGENCY
MANAGEMENT DUE TO FLOODING IN CHAVES COUNTY
WHEREAS, Chaves County was impacted by severe flooding that began on October 19,
2024, as a result of an excessive amount of rainfall in a short period of time;
WHEREAS, the flooding in Chaves County caused extensive damage to infrastructure,
homes, and businesses throughout multiple communities, including the City of Roswell;
WHEREAS, over three hundred people have required rescuing as a result of the flooding;
WHEREAS, the flooding has led to the hospitalization of at least thirty-eight people and
deaths of two people;
WHEREAS, hundreds of people have been displaced as a result of the flooding;
WHEREAS, the flooding prompted the Chaves County Board of Commissioners to orally
declare a local state of emergency;
WHEREAS, the Chaves County Board of Commissioners have indicated that all available
local resources are insufficient to address the emergency;

WHEREAS, the Chaves County Board of Commissioners requested immediate financial

aid and material assistance from the State of New Mexico;

State Capitol + Room 400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 * 505-476-2200

WHEREAS, | initially declared a state of emergency in Chaves County due to the flooding
on October 21, 2024; and

WHEREAS, the Department of Homeland Security and Emergency Management has
confirmed that it is necessary to authorize the release of additional emergency funds to protect
public peace, health, and safety.

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
DECLARE a state of emergency to exist in Chaves County due to flooding as a result of the
above-described situation, and ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. The Department of Finance and Administration shall make available emergency

FIRE AND FLOODING AND AUTHORIZING EMERGENCY FUNDS FOR THE

WHEREAS, Otero County was severely impacted by the Seven Springs Fire that began
on June 17, 2025, as well as subsequent major flooding throughout the County beginning on June

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2025-292

ORDERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF DEPUTY ANTONIO ALEMAN

Deputy Antonio Aleman of the Dona Ana County Sheriffs Office tragically lost his life in
a car crash while on duty on July 8, 2025. Deputy Aleman served with courage, integrity, and a
steadfast commitment to the safety of all New Mexicans. He will be greatly missed by his family
and community and will be remembered as a dedicated husband and father to his two children. It
is appropriate and proper to acknowledge Deputy Aleman’s life and service through a public
period of mourning across New Mexico.

NOW THEREFORE, |, Howie Morales, Lieutenant Governor of the State of New Mexico
and acting Governor pursuant to Article V, Section 7 of the New Mexico Constitution, by virtue
of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico, do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT that all United States and State flags be flown at half-staff beginning July
15, 2025, and lasting through sundown of July 20, 2025. This action will serve to commemorate
Deputy Aleman’s life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2025-414

ORDER LOWERING FLAGS TO HALF-STAFF
IN MEMORIAL OF SENATOR CLINT HARDEN

Former state senator Clint Harden passed away on October 18, 2025. Senator Harden
served eastern New Mexico with distinction for over a decade, and his good work benefited every
corner of New Mexico. He worked tirelessly advocating for children with autism and their
families, removing barriers for those reentering the workforce after being incarcerated, and
advancing early childhood education. Senator Harden was a civil leader who understood the
importance of being able to disagree without being disagreeable. Senator Harden left an indelible
mark on New Mexico, and his leadership will be missed.

NOW THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico,
do hereby ORDER and DIRECT that all United States and State flags be flown at half-staff
beginning November 8, 2025, and lasting through sundown of November 11, 2025. This action

will serve to commemorate Senator Harden’s life and to mourn his loss.

serve to commemorate Lieutenant Governor Mondragon’s life and to mourn his loss.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 2026-003

ENDING THE PRACTICE OF CHILDREN STAYING OVERNIGHT
IN CHILDREN, YOUTH AND FAMILIES DEPARTMENT OFFICES

WHEREAS, the Children, Youth and Families Department (““CYFD”) has historically
faced challenges in securing safe and appropriate placements for children and youth entering state
custody, resulting in some children staying overnight in CYFD offices;

WHEREAS, such arrangements are not appropriate or conducive to a child’s well-being;

WHEREAS, these office stays have occurred despite CYFD’s efforts to engage foster
families, kinship caregivers, shelters, and community organizations;

WHEREAS, the reasons for these overnight stays have included emergency removals of
sibling groups, behavioral health challenges, discharges from treatment facilities without available
placements, and older youth refusing placement options;

WHEREAS, CYFD leadership has implemented a comprehensive approach to end all
office stays by March of 2026, including convening cross-agency teams, engaging providers, and
establishing transitional home-like programs; and

WHEREAS, as of January 16, 2026, CYFD has ceased allowing new office stays and has
begun relocating youth to appropriate placements, with full elimination of office stays anticipated

by March of 2026.

State Capitol ° Room 400 + Santa Fe, New Mexico 87501 * 505-476-2200

NOW, THEREFORE, I, Michelle Lujan Grisham, Governor of the State of New Mexico,
by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and laws of the State of New Mexico do hereby
ORDER and DIRECT as follows:

1. Effective March 1, 2026, no child in CYFD custody shall stay overnight in any
CYFD office for any reason.

2. CYFD shall ensure that all children and youth in its care are placed in safe,
appropriate, and licensed settings designed for care and supervision, including foster homes,
kinship care, shelters, or transitional facilities.

3. CYFD shall maintain and expand collaborative efforts with providers, sister
agencies, and community organizations to secure adequate placements and prevent future office
